To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SP-B content of the lungs of immunodeficient mice infected with Pneumocystic carinii is reduced, and that this reduction is mediated at the mRNA level.
the expression of surfactant protein (SP)-B is inhibited during P. cariniii pneumonia (PCP), a common opportunistic infection in immunocompromised hosts.
the lung SP-B expression is selectively inhibited in two animal models of PCP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of P. carini pneumonia.
the pathogenesis of P. carini pneumonia (PCP), which is an opportunistic infection that occurs primarily in individuals with impaired cell-mediated immunity.
the mechanisms of lung injury in patients with AIDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

P. carini infection causes an acquired deficiency of the hydrophobic surfactant protein SP-B in mice and that this may be an important contributor of the pathogenesis of the respiratory failure associated with PCP.
the inhibition of surfactant protein expression during PCP may be an important factor in the pathogenesis of the hypoxemic lung injury associated with this infection.
Pneumocystic carinii pneumonia induces selective inhibition of SP-B in mouse models of the infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SP-B is a key protein for normal pulmonary surfactant function and that its expression is selectively inhibited during PCP.

P. carini induces selective downregulation of surfactant protein-B (SP-B), a hydrophobic surfactant-associated protein that is essential for normal surf actant function, in two mouse models for P. cariniii pneumonia.
Pneumocystic organisms can down regulate the expression of SPB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pathogenesis of P. carini pneumonia is not only a consequence of the organism itself, but also a consequence of the host response to the organism.
Pneumocystosis is associated with an acquired deficiency of the surfactant protein SP-B.
Pneumocystic pneumonia is a very serious infection that can lead to hypoxemic respiratory distress.
